chunks: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh from his uncle Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Ibn Fadhal from Abdullah ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah from his father (peace be upon him) who said:

For the adulterer are six characteristics: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, the light of the face is removed, it begets poverty, and it hastens demise. And as for those in the Hereafter, the displeasure of the Lord, the bad reckoning, and eternity in the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What are the three worldly and three Hereafter punishments for an adulterer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a comprehensive diagnostic of *zina*, illustrating how the sin corrupts both the physical vessel and the spiritual soul. The worldly triad—loss of facial radiance, poverty, and hastened death—serves as tangible signs of divine withdrawal, while the Hereafter triad emphasizes the permanence of the penalty through the specific concepts of divine displeasure (*sakhata*), rigorous accounting (*su' al-hisab*), and eternal abode in Hell.
